changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 2 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6661-app-launcher-nav-menu-renderers.md`

- names `en.ts` → `packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts` — edited by this change

  > Three new strings — the launcher's and the menu's accessible names, and the menu's empty state — are declared under `console.nav` in `en.ts` and its nine sibling packs. An inline `defaultValue` alone is not a fix: it renders English at one call site and leaves the string untranslatable everywhere (objectui#3517).

### `.changeset/7997-detail-view-related-retired.md`

- names `RecordDetailView.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **Why it retired.** `@objectstack/spec` declares no `DetailView` schema at all — every `DetailView` occurrence in `packages/spec/src` is prose about this repo's own `RecordDetailView.tsx` — so this array mirrored no protocol schema and drifted freely: it declared `columns` as `TableColumn[]` while the renderer it fed also accepted bare field names, `{ field, label }` and legacy `{ name, label }` spellings. The axis that carried the ruling was measured **zero pull**: no application code authored the member, both internal producers of a `detail-view` node (`RecordDetailDrawer`, `renderers/record-details.tsx`) synthesize it without `related`, and the only in-tree authorings carrying real columns were two documents — both rewritten here.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `5d689c3f6` (merge-base with origin/main): 12 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1708 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2311 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36468198139)

- This PR's own delta is +376 gzip bytes (+1039 raw), measured by the dev on a console build at base and at head, with 330 eager chunks on both. Of that, +319 is the `RecordDetailView` chunk: the rollback ledger that keeps a refused reaction from staying on screen. The rest is hash churn.
- No fix exists yet. Bringing `main` back under the budget is objectui#10996's to decide, and this PR's bytes are part of what it will measure.
- `Bundle Analysis` is not in the repository's required set, so this PR lands on its required checks and review. No re-run: it would read the same `main`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fd543fab661cc0d1671f04e79746490dba04d47a`

This is an in-seat review. The diff is one handler in `RecordDetailView`, three module helpers, a pin file, a changeset, and one key in each of ten locale packs (13 files, +521 −52), `Clause-②: no`, executing the seat's order on claim `5875254779`. I read the whole diff against `main` `5d689c3f6e`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The write leaves the updater.**
   - The handler finds the row on screen, computes the toggle with the pure `toggleOwnReaction`, sets it, and issues one `update` from the handler.
   - The old code issued the `update` inside the `setFeedItemsByRecord` updater. The StrictMode pin measures two writes per click on base and one on head.
   - The stored shape is moved verbatim into `storedReactionShape`: the signed-in user, then `__other__` padding, unchanged as ordered.
2. **The rollback is right for writes that each store the whole set.**
   - Every click records the set it showed as a step. A stored answer drops the older steps, because that write holds the row's whole set as of its click. A refused answer marks its step.
   - The row then shows the newest step not refused. `steps[0]` is always stored, so a target always exists.
   - I walked the cases:
     - one click refused: back to the stored set, with the toast;
     - two clicks, the earlier refused and the later still pending: nothing changes, no toast, and the later write carries the earlier click;
     - the later stored first, then the earlier refused: the earlier step is gone from the ledger, so `indexOf` is −1 and nothing happens;
     - both refused: back to the stored set;
     - a re-read replacing the row: the next click starts a fresh ledger because `shown` no longer matches, and a late answer on the old ledger finds its step missing or the row changed, so it writes nothing.
   - The dev measured the two plain options the order offered, one-off and restored, and each fails a real case. The inverse toggle takes back a reaction a later write stored; snapshot-if-unchanged leaves the first of two refused clicks on screen. So the deviation from the order's two options is measured, not taste.
3. **The handler reads the rendered row.** `feedItemsByRecord` is in the deps. React flushes discrete-event updates before the next click, so the second click of a pair reads the first click's row, and the two-click pins exercise exactly that.
4. **The toast is raised only when a rollback takes back what the user sees.** It is the localized `detail.reactionFailed`, with the key added beside `detail.commentFailed` in all ten packs, each a real translation. I read all ten lines.
5. **No data source now returns early.** Before, it toggled locally with no write. The feed is only read through a data source, so no row exists to click there. The dev states it as a deviation, and it is correct.
6. **Pins** (6 rows):
   - Base: 4 failed / 2 passed. The four fix rows are red on base: a single refusal, both refused, remove-own restored in place, and StrictMode one write.
   - The two rows green on base are the resolved control and the earlier-refused, later-stored row, which pins the chosen rollback. Ablation B (only the stored steps count) turns it red.
   - Ablation A puts back the discarding `catch` and turns exactly the three refusal rows red. Both ablations were restored to the HEAD blob.
7. **Changeset.** `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch` and `'@object-ui/i18n': patch`. Each sentence matches the code:
   - one write per click;
   - the newest set a write stored or can still store;
   - a refused click carried by a later write is kept;
   - the stored shape is unchanged.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for both packages, and `Clause-②: no` holds. The new helpers and interfaces are module-private, one catalogue key is added, and no declared type, accepted key or export moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **CI:** this record posts only after the eight required checks at `fd543fab66` are final and green. The landing queue gates on them and re-runs `git merge-tree` against current `main` first.
- **`Bundle Analysis`:** red. `main` is already over the console eager-closure ceiling (objectui#10996). This PR adds +376 gzip bytes (+1039 raw), +319 of them in the `RecordDetailView` chunk, measured by the dev on a console build at base and at head. It is not a required check. One standing-down comment says so on the PR.
- **Merge-tree (dev):** clean against `main` `e9ca14ca93`, and against PR objectui#11012's head `8fe632d960`, which edits two citation comments in the same file.
- **Out of scope, filed with this landing:** the stored shape's `__other__` padding erases every other user's reaction ids on any click. The dev measured it, it is pre-existing, and it is unchanged here as ordered. It gets its own card.
- **State:** draft, with assignee `os-elon-musk`. There is no `needs:contract-review` label, which fits `Clause-②: no`.
